name: Scrawl
label: Simple Machines
lede: Scrawl bought back its own master tapes at auction, got dropped by Elektra over a fax, and is still playing out of Columbus forty years after Marcy Mays and Sue Harshe started it.

eras.title: Skull becomes Scrawl
eras.text: Mays started Skull in Columbus; Harshe came in on bass when the band was offered an opening slot. A new name and a new drummer arrived before the Meat Puppets show, and a $500 album followed.

years.cap: The original lineup: Carolyn O'Leary, Sue Harshe and Marcy Mays
years.h: Skull becomes Scrawl in time to open for the [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]]
years.p: Drummer Carolyn O'Leary replaces Carla Sanseri before the August date. Marcy Mays drops the name Skull because it sounded too heavy metal.
years.xp:
Mays formed Skull in Columbus with bassist Jane Young and Sanseri. When promoter Curt Scheiber offered the band an opening slot for the Butthole Surfers, Young passed and Harshe joined on bass.

Harshe has said the new name also rhymed with the old one. Matter News places the Meat Puppets opening slot at Stache's.

years.cap: Marcy Mays (left) and Sue Harshe at ComFest, Columbus
years.h: Plus, Also, Too cost under $500 and caught Robert Christgau's ear
years.p: Scrawl's debut LP comes out on Curt Scheiber's No Other Records. Christgau's Village Voice review brings offers from Homestead, Twin/Tone and Rough Trade.
years.xp:
The album was recorded in September 1986 in a friend's basement, where the band had to keep the volume down because of the parents upstairs, per Matter News.

Christgau's write-up ran in his "Consumer Guide" column.

eras.title: Signed, then stranded
eras.text: Rough Trade signs Scrawl after a CBGB show Mays hated, sends the band to Prince's Paisley Park, then goes bankrupt with the masters.

years.cap: Poster for the Nov. 21, 1988 show: American Music Club, Scrawl and Amrep
years.h: Scrawl signs to Rough Trade, then cuts He's Drunk at Paisley Park
years.p: The deal came in spring 1988, after a CBGB show Mays remembers as one of the band's worst. The record was made in Minneapolis and came out in October.
years.xp:
Harshe told Matter News the band saw Prince's labeled meat refrigerator but never met him. Mays's memory of the session: "my amp was broken, and he didn't care."

Wikipedia reports the record had sold about 4,000 copies by 1990. Scrawl toured with Firehose behind it into March 1989.

yt: Scrawl live and interviewed on WNYU, 1989
years.p: Producer Gary Smith recorded it in November 1989 and Rough Trade released it in February 1990.
years.xp: Harshe called the sessions "a really bizarre recording experience" and said it was when the band "really started to come together."

years.h: Rough Trade goes under, and Scrawl buys its own tapes at auction
years.p: With the label in bankruptcy and the band's albums out of print, the master recordings went to a public auction.
years.xp: The band had already left Rough Trade that fall, after talks over a fourth album fell apart and a four-song promotional EP of covers recorded by Steve Albini went nowhere.

eras.title: Albini, and a new drummer
eras.text: Scrawl pays for its own EP, records it with Steve Albini, and loses its drummer within the year.

years.big: "We paid for this recording; we got tired of waiting for faxes, phone calls, contracts, money and bankruptcy notices."
years.p: The liner note on Scrawl's Feel Good All Over EP. The 2,000-copy first pressing sold out fast, and the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll put it ninth among EPs.
years.xp: It was recorded in January and April 1991 and released in October. The ninth-place finish was a tie with releases from Dinosaur Jr. and Prisonshake, despite poor distribution.

years.big: "We got some publicity out of it."
years.h: Scrawl plays the Kill Rock Stars festival in Olympia, 1991
years.p: Sue Harshe, asked in 1993 about riot grrrl. The festival bill had [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] and Beat Happening on it.
years.xp: At Length says the band felt too old, or too skeptical, to be comfortable in that scene. Kathleen Hanna has cited Scrawl as an influence, and Tsunami's Jenny Toomey has called them an enormous influence on how her band worked.

years.h: Carolyn O'Leary quits, and Scrawl goes acoustic
years.p: Marcy Mays and Sue Harshe tour as a duo until [[Dana Marshall|3f1a27a7-6575-426c-9d25-c83afd27ff93]] arrives on drums by the end of the year.

years.h: Dana Marshall joins on drums as Scrawl signs to Simple Machines
years.p: The deal covers Simple Machines in the US and Southern Records in the UK.

eras.title: Simple Machines picks them up
eras.text: A split single with Versus, then the record most fans call the band's best: Velvet Hammer, with Albini back at the board.

years.h: Scrawl and Versus share a Simple Machines 7-inch
years.p: Scrawl's side is "January"; Versus has the other, "Working Holiday".

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Hammer · Matter News · At Length
years.p: Recorded in January 1993 and released November 8 by Simple Machines, it opens with "Your Mother Wants to Know".
years.xp:
Harshe told Matter News Albini was the first engineer they worked with who hadn't been hired by a record label. Mays liked that he "didn't really have a dog in the race."

The New York Times wrote that Mays's guitar and Harshe's bass "sometimes stand apart, sometimes mesh for buzzing riffs"; Entertainment Weekly gave it an A-. At Length calls it the band's most downbeat record.

years.h: Reading Festival, on a European run behind Velvet Hammer
years.p: The fall 1994 tour takes Scrawl to the UK festival.

eras.title: Elektra signs them, then faxes them
eras.text: Terry Tolkin brings Scrawl to a major label. The label drops them by fax six weeks after the second album, and Dana Marshall plays his last show in 2000.

years.h: Terry Tolkin brings Scrawl to Elektra for Travel On, Rider
years.p: Released in August 1996; by August 1998 it had sold 2,115 copies.

years.big: "Disgusted. Relieved. Out of the Closet. Other."
years.h: Elektra drops Scrawl by fax, six weeks after Nature Film
years.p: The checkboxes on the postcard fans mailed to Elektra head Sylvia Rhone, with the fax printed on the other side.
years.xp:
More than 250 supporters sent one. Nature Film re-recorded six Rough Trade-era songs and a Public Image Ltd cover alongside six new ones, and sold 956 copies by August 1998.

Harshe said re-recording made sense because "the thought of giving [Elektra] 12 new songs seemed depressing to us." Cleveland Scene's David Martin filed Scrawl under the "Columbus Curse", bands signed and tossed aside by majors.

years.h: Dana Marshall plays his last show, then moves to Sweden
years.p: Mays and Harshe keep going as an acoustic pair into 2001.

eras.title: Still here
eras.text: Scrawl regroups for a club anniversary in 2007 and has kept coming back.

yt: Scrawl play "Charles" at the 5th Parking Lot Blowout, Columbus, July 10, 2010
years.h: Little Brother's tenth anniversary brings Scrawl back
years.p: The Columbus club's party is the occasion. Jovan Karcic of Gaunt takes over the drum stool, and Harshe starts Fort Shame the same year.

years.h: A free show in Franklinton, and instrumentals for a possible album
years.p: The trio had been meeting monthly since early summer. It played Secret Studio on September 30, 2023.
years.xp: Mays told Matter News the band was building a pile of instrumental material toward an eventual new record.

years.h: Tsunami's Luther Gray sits in at DromFest
years.p: Jovan Karcic couldn't make the 2025 festival in Catskill, New York, so [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]]'s Gray took the drums. The band had also played DromFest in 2024.
years.xp: Harshe called Gray "super enthusiastic and a real mensch throughout this entire endeavor." On the band's staying power she told Psychedelic Baby: "What I love about that is today I still see and listen to some of the same friends I did in 1985."
